answer: Hardware-rooted reward quotas bind payouts to an attested device identity rather than login names. The verifier checks a manufacturer certificate and debits one device budget: a thread signing as nebula and another as tide share that cap. N independent budgets require N certified devices, so an attacker must buy or rent additional hardware; extra names alone earn nothing. This depends on one stable identity per device. Resettable IDs, forged certificates or compromised attestation break the bound.
